intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GABRB1 gene (137190) on chromosome 4p12.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GABRB1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Despite lack of association with epilepsy syndromes, our results suggest GABRB1 as a candidate human epilepsy gene.
checks.explanation: Paper reports a de novo heterozygous GABRB1 mutation in an IS patient and suggests GABRB1 as a candidate epilepsy gene, but does not name DEE45 or establish causation.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 gene is located on chromosome 4p12.
checks.evidence_quote: four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature for the gene discussed in the paper. The paper itself does not state it.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 is a severe neurologic disorder that begins in infancy. The reported seizure types include infantile spasms and the migrating focal seizures of epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS). Affected individuals can have severe developmental impairment and hypotonia.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 is a severe neurologic disorder with onset in infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: Epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS) is a rare, devastating developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) characterized by seizure migration between cerebral hemispheres and profound developmental impairment
checks.explanation: Severe DEE with onset in the first six months of life.

checks.claim: Seizure types reported in developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 include infantile spasms.
checks.evidence_quote: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
checks.explanation: The GABRB1 patient had infantile spasms.

checks.claim: Seizure types reported in developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 include the migrating focal seizures of epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS).
checks.explanation: The GABRB1 patient is part of the EIMFS cohort.

checks.claim: Individuals with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 can have severe developmental impairment.
Individuals with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 can have hypotonia.
checks.explanation: H = hypotonia in the motor disorders column.

paragraphs.text: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) screened for de novo mutations in patients with 2 classic epileptic encephalopathies, infantile spasms (149 patients) and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (115 patients). One patient in this cohort, who had 1 of these 2 epileptic encephalopathies, carried a de novo GABRB1 mutation.

paragraphs.text: Burgess et al. (2019) studied a cohort of 135 patients with EIMFS. One of them (patient 63) had a de novo GABRB1 variant. This patient had seizure onset at 4 months of age, with focal seizures at onset. At last report, at 2 years of age, the patient had profound to severe developmental impairment and hypotonia. Burgess et al. (2019) noted that the GABRB1 phenotypic spectrum now extended to EIMFS, and they emphasized a role for GABA-related mechanisms in this disorder.

paragraphs.text: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) sequenced the exomes of 264 trios in which the child had infantile spasms or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. Six patients had de novo mutations in GABA-A receptor subunit genes: 4 in GABRB3 and 1 each in GABRA1 and GABRB1. The GABRB1 mutation was confirmed by Sanger sequencing in the trio and was absent from both parents. They suggested that individual rare mutations in different genes may converge on shared pathways.

paragraphs.text: Janve et al. (2016) carried out a functional study of a de novo heterozygous phe246-to-ser (F246S) mutation in the GABRB1 gene, which had been identified in a patient with infantile spasms. In HEK293T cells, the mutation caused only a minor reduction (about 25%) in GABA-evoked peak current in the homozygous expression condition, and no change in the heterozygous condition. However, it slowed current deactivation and increased single-channel mean open time and burst duration. Mutant receptors opened spontaneously, with a 4-fold increase in spontaneous open probability and increased holding currents. Surface levels of the mutant beta-1 subunit were slightly reduced, while total levels were unchanged.

checks.evidence_quote: Since the LGS and IS patients were heterozygous for the de novo GABRB3 and GABRB1 mutations, we also studied α1β1,3γ2L receptors containing these mutations
checks.explanation: Functional study of de novo heterozygous GABRB1(F246S).

paragraphs.text: Burgess et al. (2019) used whole-exome sequencing in a cohort of 135 patients with EIMFS. In 1 patient they identified a de novo heterozygous ile247-to-thr (I247T) variant in the GABRB1 gene (Chr4:47405633T-C). The variant was absent from the ExAC and gnomAD databases and was classified as likely pathogenic. GABRB1 was 1 of 9 genes newly implicated in EIMFS.

paragraphs.text: Janve et al. (2016) suggested that the faster rise time and slower deactivation caused by the GABRB1 F246S mutation would lengthen the first inhibitory postsynaptic current (IPSC). They proposed that it would also reduce charge transfer during later IPSCs, causing a net loss of GABAergic inhibition. They suggested GABRB1 as a candidate human epilepsy gene.
